notes.decision: Lines 8 and 10 contain scribal cancellations of ⲕⲁ (= 21). The scribe was apparently writing the chapter number 21 for the new kephalaion that begins at line 12, with multiple corrections in the heading area. Treated as lacuna since the canceled text does not represent the intended reading.
Translated 'the two Callings.' Distinct from the Call/Hearing pair — two summonings/emanations are distinguished here. The verb ⲉⲧⲁϩⲧⲁⲍⲙⲟⲩ confirms the act of summoning forth.

Three measure-terms: ⲉϩⲁⲧ 'silver' (used metonymically as 'weight/balance'), ϣⲓ 'measure,' Greek μέτρον 'metron.' Reads as triplet of measuring-instruments — pointing to what cannot be measured even by these.

ⲕⲗⲏⲗ rendered 'wreaths' from the Coptic root ⲕⲗⲟⲙ 'wreath/garland,' here probably 'produce, growth' of the earth in pairing with 'clusters of vines.' Confirmed by line 26 collocation ⲃⲝⲃⲓⲗⲉ ⲛ̄ϣⲱ 'grains of sand' as parallel small-thing register.
'Clusters of the vines' — ⲝⲗⲟⲗⲉ = ϫⲗⲟⲗⲉ 'grape-cluster'; ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩⲉⲩⲉ = Lyc. plural of ⲉⲗⲟⲟⲗⲉ 'vine.'

'The three rivers'; ⲙⲁⲝⲓⲟⲣⲉ likely Lyc. orthographic variant for 'rivers' (with ⲓⲟⲣ 'river' as core) — possibly 'places of rivers' or compound river-noun. Standard Manichaean cosmology has three or four cosmic rivers surrounding the world.

ⲙⲉⲥⲗⲏⲥ rendered 'limbs' (μέλη with anomalous Lyc. orthography). ⲉⲧϣⲙⲁⲁⲧ provisionally 'dispersed/scattered'; alternative 'honored' from ⲧⲁⲉⲓⲏⲩ is also possible. The dispersed light-limbs are a standard Manichaean cosmological motif.
'Grains/kernels' — paired with ⲛϣⲱ 'sand' in line 26 as small-particle measure. Distinct from ⲡⲃⲣⲉ 'seed.' Likely related to ⲃⲣⲃⲣ 'pebble' or a granular-dimensional term.
'They shall not be likened to him' — ϣⲧⲏⲧⲉ from ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲛ 'liken, compare,' Lyc. infinitive form with ϣ- circumstantial. ⲁϩⲣ̄ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ = 'as before / as previously.'
ⲥⲉⲍⲉ 'set/raise' + ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲥ̄ 'on her feet' — the standard idiom 'cause her to stand up' (cf. ⲥⲉⲍⲱ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ in accumulated vocabulary). Used here of the Mother(?) being established within his storehouses.
'Stillness and silence' — the ⲍⲣⲁⲕ/ⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓⲧϩ pair appears elsewhere as the calm-state of pre-emanation. The Mother dwells in the storehouses in this state until summoned.
'She gazed upon' — ⲃⲱϣⲧ 'look, gaze' + ⲥⲁ 'after, upon.' The Mother surveying her own aeons of light upon emanation.

Tentatively rendered 'in death.' ⲧⲙⲟ is unusual; likely Lycopolitan ⲧⲙⲟⲩ ('the death,' fem. of ⲡⲙⲟⲩ) or possibly ⲧⲙⲁ 'the place.' Context — 'doing a great time being established in X, standing fast in their...' — fits the death/abyss into which First Man descended. The companion phrase ⲉϩⲧⲁϩⲥ̄ ('being fixed/anointed') with ⲉϩⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ ('standing fast') suggests cosmological captivity within the dark realm.

Translated 'battle' on the assumption that this is a continuation across line-break (line 7 ⲁ- + line 8 ⲡⲁⲧⲱⲛ → ⲁⲡⲁⲧⲱⲛ) of a battle/contest noun, parallel to ⲡⲁⲣⲱⲛ in accumulated vocabulary. Could alternatively be a different form. The cosmic battle (πόλεμος/ἀγών) of First Man fits the context.

Translated 'that shine forth.' Reading as ⲉⲧ-ⲡⲓⲉ-ⲱⲩ from the verbal root ⲡⲓⲉ 'shine, radiate' (already in glossary as the root of ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance'). Applied to the Five Gods who are sons. Alternative reading 'that are great' (= ⲡⲱⲟⲩ) is also possible.

Translated 'delay much.' ⲣ̄-ⲉⲥⲕⲉ from ⲱⲥⲕ 'tarry, delay'; ϩⲁⲧ likely intensifier 'much, long.' The ϯ- forms are unusual — possibly errors for ⲛ̄- or definite article. Context (in the First Man) supports temporal delay of the Five Gods within him.

Tentatively parsed 'she sent her.' The verb ⲟⲩⲱⲣⲥ̄ (= ⲟⲩⲱⲣⲡ 'send') with prefix; the sequence ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲥ-ⲟⲩⲣ-ⲟⲩⲱⲣⲥ̄ would mean 'when she sent her' or similar. The line establishes that the Mother of Life was sent down by the Father — fits Manichaean cosmology of her cosmic descent.

Translated 'the place of the Twelve Aeons.' ⲙⲁⲛ̄ⲧⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥ̄ = 'place of the twelfth/twelve' — the next line continues with [ⲛⲁⲩ]ⲥ̄ confirming -ⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥ̄ 'twelve.' The Twelve Aeons hidden behind the veil of light is a standard Manichaean cosmological grouping.
Translated 'glance of the eye.' ϩⲣⲁⲡⲣⲉⲡ likely = ϣⲣⲁⲡⲣⲉⲡ 'twinkle, blink' (cf. Sah. ⲣⲡⲉ-ⲣⲡⲉ); ⲃⲉⲗ = ⲃⲁⲗ 'eye.' The biblical idiom 'in the twinkling of an eye' (1 Cor 15:52) fits.
Translated 'the Mother of Life' — standard Manichaean cosmological figure (consort/companion of First Man). The collocation ⲙⲉⲩ + ⲡⲱⲛⲍ is the technical title.

Tentatively analyzed as ⲁϥ-ϫⲱⲕ-ⲥ̄ 'he perfected/completed her' (Lyc. ⲭ for ϫ; ϫⲱⲕ 'fulfill, perfect' + 3sg.f suffix). Parallel verb ⲁϩⲕⲁⲁⲥ ('he set her') in same line supports a verb-of-establishment reading.
ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ = Lyc. ⲧⲱϩⲙ̄ 'call forth, summon' — the technical Manichaean verb of serial emanation (cf. accumulated vocab). The Five Sons are 'called forth' from the First Man.
Parsed as ⲭⲉ (= ϫⲉ 'that') + ⲉⲩⲛⲁ-ⲣ̄ⲡⲣⲟ 'they will reign' (future III, Lyc. ⲡⲡⲣⲟ for ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ via assimilation). The reduplication ⲡ̄ⲡ̄ is a scribal feature of Lycopolitan.
ⲍⲁⲕϩ̄ = ϩⲱⲕ 'strip' + suffix (cf. ⲁϩϩⲱⲕ in accumulated vocab); ⲙⲁⲣϩ̄ = ⲙⲟⲩⲣ 'bind' + suffix. Twin-verb sequence 'stripped him, bound him' fits the cosmological-mythic register of capture.
Translated 'the Stillness' per accumulated vocabulary — Manichaean technical term, also a name of the Fast.
Greek φορεῖν 'to wear, bear' — First Man wears his Five Sons as armor before descending into battle. Standard Manichaean cosmogonic detail (cf. five storehouses/garments = Five Light Elements).
ⲧⲱϩ = 'mingling, joining' (cf. ⲧⲱⲍⲙ in vocab); with ⲙⲉⲑⲟⲣⲓⲟⲛ 'boundary' yields 'a joining of boundaries' — the cosmological line where the regions meet.

ⲉⲥⲕⲉ likely Lyc. infinitive of ⲱⲥⲕ 'tarry, delay, prolong (time)'. ⲣ̄- + noun = 'spend a tarrying' = 'tarried, lingered.' The pairing ⲣ̄ ⲟⲩⲕⲁⲓⲣⲟⲥ ⲙⲛ ⲟⲩⲭⲣⲟⲛⲟⲥ ('spent a season and a time') in lines 18-19 frames the same kind of temporal-extension idiom.

ⲧⲃⲁⲧ tentatively rendered 'cubit' (a measure-noun); ϣⲓ = 'measure'. The phrase 'number of cubits of the measure of those who mount upon them' fits a cosmological accounting of the wind/breath-vehicles' span.
ⲛⲓϩ = 'breath, wind' (Sah. ⲛⲓϥⲉ). The breaths/winds that come down into the cosmos are the cosmological wind-element vehicles.

ⲧⲱⲟⲩ 'mountain' + relative clause 'of those who serve/praise.' ϣⲉⲩⲉ tentatively rendered 'serve' (cf. ϣⲙϣⲉ 'serve, worship'). The First Man stands on a 'mountain of those who serve' until the descent to combat.

ⲡⲁⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'the glorious one' (per vocab); ⲥⲛⲏⲩⲧ qualitative of ⲥⲛⲏⲩⲧⲉ 'flow forth, emanate.' Construction: 'the gods of the glorious one who are emanated' — the gods belonging to the Father of Greatness who flow forth from him.

Greek ζωγραφέω 'paint, depict from life' — the cosmogonic verb whereby the Father of Greatness 'depicts' (calls into manifest cosmic form) each emanation. Same verb earlier used of Matter painting herself; here used of Light's positive depiction. Preserves the iconic-creative semantics.
Greek loanword καιρός 'appointed time, decisive moment.' Translated 'moment' to capture the punctual sense, not generic 'time.'

Per accumulated vocabulary 'depart upward / be raised up / ascend.' Here used of the primordial Darkness ascending against the Light at the cosmogonic onset — the foundational event narrated retrospectively in this kephalaion.

ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'reveal/uncover forth' (Crum 'reveal, uncover'); functions like ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ. Recurs four times on this page (lines 18, 22, 27, 32) as the technical verb for the Father's eschatological self-disclosure.
'His hidden storehouses' — the cosmic ⲧⲁⲙⲓⲟⲛ (already in vocab) into which the gathered powers withdraw at the consummation. The hiddenness language (ⲍⲏⲡ) marks the eschatological storehouse motif.
Causative ⲥⲉⲍⲉ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'set on the feet of' (cf. accumulated ⲥⲉⲍⲱ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'set on his feet'). Each cosmic being is set upright in its proper place at the eschatological reordering.
Standard prophetic-apocalyptic formula 'what has happened and what shall happen.' The apostles' commission spans both retrospective and predictive disclosure.
Feminine 'the first (one),' likely referring to the primordial event — the first cosmogonic moment (the depiction of all things by the Father, line 1) which the apostles are commissioned to declare.

Per accumulated vocabulary: Lycopolitan plural of ⲓⲱⲧ 'father' = 'all the Fathers,' i.e. the divine emanations. The page closes on a phrase that opens a new sentence about the time of all the Fathers.

Translated 'established forth' preserving the spatial-emanative semantics of ⲥⲙⲛ + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ. The subject (feminine: 'she') refers to a figure (likely the divine cosmological structure or Wisdom) whose existence extends 'unto the aeons.'
ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ idiom = 'stand fast.' Substantivized with possessive: 'their standing-fast' = their firm foundation/stability.
ⲧϣⲱϥ from ϣⲱϥ 'destruction, ruin' — translated 'destruction' preserving the eschatological register paired with ⲧϩⲁⲏ 'end.'

Standard Manichaean dyad: Matter (ϩⲩⲗⲏ) and the enthumēsis (intent/inclination) of Death. Translated ⲉⲛⲑⲩⲙⲏⲥⲓⲥ as 'enthumēsis' preserving its Greek technical sense (cf. counsel = ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ in five-faculty system, also Greek ἐνθύμησις per Polotsky/Böhlig).
ⲧⲁⲙⲓⲟⲛ 'storehouse' (Greek ταμεῖον). The five storehouses of the Five Light Elements in Manichaean cosmology, here applied to Matter's own counter-storehouses.

'Her five elements' — feminine subject (Matter) and her five dark elements, mirroring the Five Light Elements. The chapter traces Matter's procession through her five-fold cosmic phases (elements → trees → fruits → demons of five worlds).

Two Greek temporal terms preserved as a doublet: καιρός (the appointed/qualitative time) + χρόνος (durational time). Translated 'time and chronos' to preserve the technical distinction; this pair recurs throughout the page as the technical structure of Matter's temporal phases.

Reading ⲍⲱⲣⲡⲁϥⲉ/ϩⲱⲣⲡⲁϥⲉ as 'bring forth' (cf. accumulated vocab note: possibly Lyc. for ϣⲱⲣⲡ 'arrange, establish, sweep clean'). In agricultural-cosmological context with ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'fruits' as object, the productive sense 'bring forth/produce' fits best. The verb recurs four times (l.24, 25, 27 in finite; l.30 in nominal).
ⲁⲓϣ = ⲟⲉⲓϣ 'time, period.' ⲉⲛⲁϣⲱϥ = 'great, abundant' (qualitative of ⲁϣⲁⲓ). 'A great period' or 'a long time.'

Lexeme uncertain. In context (paired with demons in l.30, the falling-upon-earth mythology in l.31), this likely names a class of fallen beings — possibly giants, abortions, or another Manichaean cosmological class. Marked tentative pending parallels.

ⲥⲁⲛⲉϣ = 'nourish, rear' (accumulated vocab). The continuation from l.31's broken end into 'nourished' suggests the demons/giants are being nourished or are doing the nourishing. The recurrence in l.33 ('until they nourish the middle...') confirms.

Translated as '1468' — the standard Manichaean number for the duration of the cosmic conflagration. ⲙⲛⲧ- prefix on ⲁϥⲧⲉ̄ here functions numerically: the Great Fire burns for 1,468 years. This is the canonical Manichaean figure preserved in multiple sources.
Rendered 'the release' = ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'the dissolution' from accumulated vocabulary. ⲃⲓⲛ-/ⲟⲓⲛ- variants both form action-nouns from ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ. Eschatological cosmic-dissolution term.

Following accumulated vocabulary entry: 'prison/fastness' or possibly = ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ (Greek ζώνη, 'zone/girdle') — fitting the Manichaean motif of the cosmos as zodiacal prison. Left as 'prison/zone' to preserve ambiguity.
Variant of ⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ 'depict, paint' (already in vocabulary). The Last Extraction (ⲡⲁⲛⲁⲣⲉⲓⲁⲥ ⲛ̄ϩⲁⲉ) is the eschatological Image — the Andrias-Statue produced by 'painting' the gathered light.
Likely = ⲥⲉⲡⲉ 'remainder, residue.' The Light is separated 'out from the residue' of all things — i.e., from the residual matter. Alternative reading 'fire' (ⲥⲉⲧⲉ) less likely given context.

ⲡⲟⲩⲣⲁ tentatively read as 'their measure/portion' (ⲟⲩⲱⲣⲁ) paired with ⲱⲭⲛⲉ 'fail, cease' (accumulated vocab). Alternative: ⲡⲟⲩⲣⲁⲛ 'their name' shall fail. Either fits the eschatological-decline context.
Verb form unidentified. Possibly relates to ⲕⲓⲙ 'move' (ⲁⲥ-ⲕⲓⲙ-ⲧⲥ̄ 'she moved/disturbed it') or to ⲕⲱⲙⲧ̄ 'gather' (accumulated vocab). Left untranslated and flagged.
Translated 'she is forever' — the predication of eternal duration to a feminine entity (likely Matter/Hyle bound in the bōlos). The construction is OY-(noun)-ⲧⲉ + ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏϩⲉ 'unto eternity.'
Read as ⲁ-ⲧ-ⲙⲣⲡⲉ 'into the bond,' where ⲙⲣⲡⲉ is a Lycopolitan variant of ⲙⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'bond, fetter.' Confirmed by line 8 ⲟⲩⲙⲣⲡⲉ ⲧⲉ ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏϩⲉ 'she is a bond forever.'

Translated 'the middle' — taking ⳨ here as orthographic variant of ⲧ (definite article), giving ⲧⲙⲏⲧⲉ. Elsewhere on the page ⳨ functions as ϯ ('5') in ⲡ⳨ⲟⲩ; the dialect is inconsistent in its use of this character.
